children: The BSE Sensex falls 1,605.44 points, or 2.15 per cent, while the NSE Nifty declines 546.15 points, or 2.36 per cent this week

The combined market capitalisation of eight of India's 10 most valuable listed companies declined by Rs 1.56 lakh crore last week, with HDFC Bank and Bajaj Finance accounting for the largest erosion in investor wealth amid a broad-based sell-off in equities.

The decline came during a holiday-shortened trading week in which benchmark indices registered sharp losses. The BSE Sensex fell 1,605.44 points, or 2.15 per cent, while the NSE Nifty declined 546.15 points, or 2.36 per cent.

“Indian equities endured a challenging, holiday-shortened week, with benchmark indices extending their losses as inflation concerns intensified following a fresh surge in crude oil prices. Against this backdrop, rising domestic yields placed equity valuation premiums under renewed scrutiny, weighing steadily on the market and overshadowing support from resilient Q2 earnings,” said Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments.

The broader market rout also dragged down the overall valuation of BSE-listed companies. Their combined market capitalisation fell by Rs 20,78,774.28 crore over four trading sessions to Rs 4,51,83,393.14 crore, compared with Rs 4,72,62,167.42 crore on 16 October.

Among the 10 most valuable companies, eight saw their market capitalisation decline by a combined Rs 1,55,671.9 crore. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Larsen & Toubro (L&T) were the only two firms to register valuation gains.
HDFC Bank, Bajaj Finance Bear Brunt Of Sell-off

HDFC Bank recorded the steepest decline in market value among the top 10 companies, with its valuation falling by Rs 55,506.95 crore to Rs 10,67,121.12 crore. Its shares declined 5 per cent during the week.
Bajaj Finance followed, losing Rs 34,180.51 crore in market capitalisation to end at Rs 5,77,146.21 crore.
Reliance Industries saw its valuation shrink by Rs 27,065.08 crore to Rs 16,10,372.11 crore, while Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) lost Rs 21,062.24 crore to Rs 4,81,142.58 crore.
Bharti Airtel's market capitalisation declined by Rs 9,360.75 crore to Rs 11,79,454.70 crore. State Bank of India (SBI) shed Rs 4,338.46 crore in valuation to Rs 8,83,384.38 crore.
Infosys lost Rs 2,881.38 crore in market value to Rs 4,68,528.03 crore, while ICICI Bank's valuation fell by Rs 1,276.53 crore to Rs 10,01,594.91 crore.
TCS and L&T bucked the broader market trend, adding to their market capitalisation during the week.
TCS recorded a valuation increase of Rs 23,517.56 crore to Rs 9,14,652.52 crore, while L&T added Rs 1,788.66 crore to reach Rs 5,01,513.72 crore.
Despite the weekly losses, Reliance Industries retained its position as India's most valuable listed company, followed by Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank. ICICI Bank ranked fourth, ahead of TCS and SBI.
Bajaj Finance, L&T, LIC and Infosys completed the list of the 10 most valuable companies.
